title: Async assertions
summary: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished.
introduction: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("reads a label", async () => { const load = async () => "ready"; await expect(load()).resolves.toBe("ready"); });
blocks.title: Async assertions

blocks.text: The promise resolves to ready, so the test passes.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Return a different label and update the expectation.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: An unawaited promise can hide a failure after the test finishes.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
